Name: Arjun Narayanan
Question: What would you advise a 5th year PhD, with no publications, wanting to pursue an academic career?
Answer: Going into the academic career track with no publications is near impossible. You’ll need to do a postdoc or two to bring your publication record to a decent length, so start looking into that. Think about what your research interests are, and based on that, identify who you would like to work with. Then talk to your professor and learn about his/her network and who his/her contacts are, and see if there is any intersection between the two groups. Hopefully there will be! If not, try networking on your own at conferences and other meetings.

Name: Arjun Narayanan
Question: Is USC's alumni network really as amazing as it sounds? What are some ways people have benefited from the network? What makes the culture so conducive to networking? Have you ever received any advantage in your career by simply being a Trojan?
Answer: It’s fantastic if you’re in business, communication, or any of the subjects that USC is famous for, but pretty much useless in the sciences, such as chemistry. I remember while at USC, we would see the Viterbi Career Fair twice a year from our chemistry building (LHI), and wonder why the chemistry department could not organize something similar for the chemistry graduate students. I have not benefited from the Trojan network, because it is not very strong in the industries I’m interested in (pharma and biotech).

Name: Arjun Narayanan
Question: PhD Careers: Would professors take on a postdoc in a topic area that's new to the postdoc?
Answer: In principle, they should, because a postdoc is supposed to be a training period where one can learn something new, which may or may not be related to the subject of the PhD. However, due to oversaturation and overproduction of PhD’s these days, professors can just pick someone with the exact skills and background they need, and this way they do not have to worry about training the new postdoc. In my experience, it is becoming rarer and rarer to see scientists switching to a new field in their postdoc after the PhD, for this very reason.

Name: Arjun Narayanan
Question: Is it a good idea to do a Ph.D. after a master’s in chemistry or to get some experience in the pharma industry and then go for a Ph.D. in pharmaceutics?
Answer: When you’re in the market looking for a job, you’ll learn this truth: Work experience trumps education, 100% of the time. If you have the opportunity to get some work experience under your belt now, do it. The added advantage is that you’ll also make some money. You can always go back to school later if you find you’re hitting a ceiling at work and the degree is necessary for promotion.

Question: Has your writing improved since joining Quora? If so, how?
Answer: Yes, but let me clarify: Writing on Quora has made me better at communicating to people on Quora. There’s a certain format that people here have come to expect, and the answers that are highly viewed or upvoted consistently stick to this. The best answers are short, inflammatory, and sacrifice detail for brevity and punch.
